s: A royal mosque named for a queen, facing the fishing port
w: Completed in 2017 and dedicated by King Mohammed VI the next year, this mosque on Tangier's fishing port is named for his grandmother, Lalla Abla bint Tahar, echoing the Mohammed V Mosque, dedicated to her husband 35 years earlier. Spread across 5,712 square metres, it holds over 1,900 worshippers, replacing a smaller Port Mosque nearby.

s: The 'Spanish Cathedral' seat of Tangier's archdiocese
w: Tangier's Catholics know it simply as the Spanish Cathedral, though its official name is the Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception and the Holy Spirit. It serves as the seat of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Tangier, proof that this port city's religious landscape runs well beyond its mosques and synagogues.

s: Built (so the story goes) to out-tower the cathedral
w: Completed in 1983 for the future Mohammed VI and named after his grandfather, who gave a landmark 1947 address here, this mosque was funded by Kuwait, and the square out front is still Place du Koweit. Local lore says a Kuwaiti sheikh, needled that the cathedral's bell tower dominated the skyline, paid up so a minaret would out-top it.
